newsitem.title: GERMANY: Lower German cocoa prices fail to tempt buyers.
newsitem.headline: Lower German cocoa prices fail to tempt buyers.

text.p: German cocoa consumers shrugged off lower bean prices this week as a result of more favourable sterling levels against the mark, traders said on Wednesday.
"It's quiet apart from a few spot purchases here and there, processors continue to live hand-to-mouth," one said.
"The arrival of Ivorian and Nigerian supplies is imminent and this paralyses the market."
The start of the Ivory Coast marketing season is expected next week.
Traders said the prospect was weighing down West African differentials for October-January arrivals, which offset technically-inspired futures advances.
Local bean prices were at 2.27 marks/kg for fourth quarter, down 0.07 on the week, and at 2.32 marks for first quarter 1997, down 0.06.
The cocoa butter ratios were nearly unchanged, with 1996 dates at 2.84, with implied butter prices liquid ex-works at 6.59 marks, off 0.14.
The first quarter 1997 ratio was 2.74 and the mark price 6.51 versus 6.59 previously.
